editorial_note: This site does not endorse any candidate or party. Candidate profiles are drawn from candidates' own statements as published in the Pelham Examiner and other publicly available information. All candidates in each race are presented using the same template. The amount of information shown reflects the public record available at time of publishing and does not indicate the importance or strength of a candidate's campaign. Register to vote by {{fact:voter-registration-deadline}} — see how this site works.

voter_info.label: Register by
voter_info.note: In person or online by October 24. By mail, postmarked by October 19 and received by October 24. Deadlines at elections.ny.gov

voter_info.label: Early voting
voter_info.note: Saturday October 24 through Sunday November 1. Hours and sites: Westchester County Board of Elections

voter_info.label: Where to vote
voter_info.note: Polling places move between elections, so check yours rather than trusting last time: voterlookup.elections.ny.gov. Voting by mail? Apply for an absentee or early mail ballot at elections.ny.gov.

races.title: Board of Trustees
races.context: Context: Hanan Eldahry, who has served since 2018, is not seeking reelection. Fiscal management is a major issue discussed by candidates and covered in local reporting — the village passed a {{fact:village-budget-fy2627}} budget with a {{fact:village-budget-increase-fy2627}} increase, overriding the state tax cap for the first time. Three seats are up; top three vote-getters win.

races.title: Board of Trustees
races.context: Context: Maurice Owen-Michaane is stepping down after three two-year terms. The 2025 Manor election was historically close — Lapey won the mayoral race by 20 votes, Case won by 2 after a recount. Kurtz returns for a rematch. Top two vote-getters win.

races.title: Town Supervisor & Town Clerk
races.badge: Re-run required by new state law
races.note: A new state law shifts odd-year municipal elections to even years. As a result, Supervisor Mohan and Clerk Miller — both elected in November 2025 — must run again in 2026 to secure full two-year terms.
races.context: Context: Mohan defeated Republican Dan McLaughlin 2,115 to 1,456 in 2025. Miller defeated Borsella 2,108 to 1,457. Both races were decided by similar margins. Town Council seats (Burke, McLoughlin, Jenks, Curtin — 4-year terms) are not up in 2026.

candidates.name: Russell Solomon
candidates.meta: Incumbent · First elected 2020 · Seeking a third term

profile.background: A Village of Pelham trustee since 2020, seeking a third two-year term. He has served as board liaison for pedestrian safety, the Department of Public Works and downtown business. In his own account of his record he championed the village-wide 25 mph speed limit, supported hiring a Traffic Safety Officer, and worked on sewer infrastructure, with more than two miles of pipes repaired.
profile.why_running: He points to a record built on direct contact with residents and on following through on the concerns they raise.
profile.prior_service: Village of Pelham Board of Trustees, 2020 to present.
quotes: I’ve made it a point to sit down directly with neighbors, local groups and business owners, understand what they need from their village government, and follow through.

profile.background: Finishing her first term as a Village of Pelham trustee, first elected in 2024. During the term she supported hiring a Traffic Safety Officer, advocated for the village at county and state level, and worked with neighbouring municipalities on quality-of-life issues. She describes three core principles guiding her work: respect, empathy and action.
profile.why_running: She says there is unfinished work ahead on infrastructure, storm resiliency, safety, local business and village communication.
profile.prior_service: Village of Pelham Board of Trustees, 2024 to present.
quotes: I am seeking re-election because there is still important work ahead — strengthening infrastructure, making serious headway on storm resiliency, improving public and pedestrian safety, supporting local businesses, enhancing village-wide communication, and ensuring that every resident feels seen, heard, and valued.

candidates.name: Kristen Burke
candidates.meta: Town Council Member · General Counsel, Mercy University

profile.background: An attorney who serves as General Counsel at Mercy University. She currently sits on the Town of Pelham Town Council on a four-year term running through 2027, and has said she would step down from that seat if elected to the Village board.
profile.why_running: She argues the Village board lacks the legal expertise the Town board has.
profile.prior_service: Town of Pelham Town Council, term through 2027.
quotes: One of the reasons I am running for Village Trustee is that currently, while there are three attorneys serving on the Town Board, along with a Town attorney, there are none on the Village board.

profile.background: An attorney at Latham & Watkins who ran for the Village of Pelham board in 2019. He signed the joint Neighborhood Party platform alongside Rhett Speros and Paul Anzilotti.
profile.why_running: He says the village has reached a “tipping point” and that decisions taken unanimously by the current board have overextended its finances. He cites debt growth from {{fact:village-debt-2021}} in 2021 to {{fact:village-debt-2026}} by early 2026, and a $3.655M Municipal Center authorization that included $800K for furniture.
profile.prior_service: No prior elected office. Ran for the Village of Pelham board in 2019.
priorities: Serve as a trustee without pay
Vote against exceeding the state tax cap
Open up the Picture House RFQ
quotes: The current board’s unanimous actions have dangerously stretched the Village’s finances.
The Village’s current path is unsustainable.

profile.background: A Pelham resident since 2007 with two children in the district’s high schools. He signed the joint Neighborhood Party platform alongside Arthur Long and Paul Anzilotti.
profile.why_running: He runs on affordability and on budget management following successive increases in property taxes.
priorities: Serve as a trustee without pay
Vote against exceeding the state tax cap
Open up the Picture House RFQ
quotes: Our village should be a place where residents can afford to stay.
The Village’s current path is unsustainable.

profile.background: A Pelham resident for more than 50 years, the last 12 of them in the Village. He signed the joint Neighborhood Party platform alongside Arthur Long and Rhett Speros, which faults undisciplined spending including the $3.655M Municipal Center authorization.
profile.why_running: He frames the campaign around village debt, saying he has “18 million reasons” for running — one for each dollar of outstanding village debt.
priorities: Serve as a trustee without pay
Vote against exceeding the state tax cap
Open up Village decisions to residents
quotes: The deficit is on a trajectory that is unsustainable without continuous substantial tax increases.
The Village’s current path is unsustainable.

profile.background: Deputy Mayor and Police Commissioner of the Village of Pelham Manor, and a member of the board since 2018. She is running with Joe Liberatore on the Neighborhood Party line and has also filed on the Republican line.
profile.prior_service: Village of Pelham Manor Board of Trustees, 2018 to present. Currently Deputy Mayor and Police Commissioner.

profile.background: A member of the Village of Pelham Manor Zoning Board of Appeals. This is his first run for elective office. He is running alongside Breda Bennett on the Neighborhood Party and Republican lines.
profile.prior_service: No prior elected office. Appointed member of the Pelham Manor Zoning Board of Appeals.

profile.background: He ran for the Pelham Manor board in November 2025 and lost to incumbent Tim Case by two votes after a manual recount, one of the closest results in Manor history. He is running again in 2026 alongside Chris Dlutkowski.
profile.prior_service: No prior elected office. Ran for the Pelham Manor Board of Trustees in 2025.

profile.background: He announced his candidacy in June 2026 and is running alongside Ryan Kurtz on the Democratic line.

candidates.name: Theresa Mohan
candidates.meta: Incumbent Town Supervisor · First woman elected to the role · Attorney

profile.background: Elected Town Supervisor in November 2025, becoming the first woman to hold the position. An attorney by training, she has served as General Counsel and Head of Human Resources for organisations of more than 15,000 people and currently teaches leadership and ethics at Fordham Law School. She previously served three terms as a Village of Pelham trustee, and says that during that tenure she helped secure grants that expanded the village’s sustainability goals without raising taxes.
profile.why_running: She is returning to the ballot less than a year into her term because a change in New York State law moves odd-year municipal elections to even years. She describes her first nine months as focused on financial systems modernisation, facilities planning and improving resident access to Town government.
profile.prior_service: Town Supervisor, 2025 to present. Village of Pelham Board of Trustees, three terms.
quotes: Pelham deserves leaders who won’t just maintain what we have, but who will plan boldly for what comes next.

profile.why_running: She is returning to the ballot less than a year into her term because a change in New York State law moves odd-year municipal elections to even years.
quotes: My experiences will strengthen and enhance communication with town officials.

candidates.name: Scott Wolfgang
candidates.meta: Challenger · Running for Supervisor · Neighborhood Party

profile.background: He launched a joint campaign with Maureen Borsella in August 2026 on the Neighborhood Party line, running for Town Supervisor.
profile.why_running: He runs on fiscal restraint, arguing that the Town should not add to the tax and debt burden residents already carry from other local municipalities.
quotes: We have significant tax and debt growth across most of our other local municipalities and it’s imperative that the Town not become yet another financial burden to our taxpayers.

Pelham’s future deserves thoughtful planning. Growth should be balanced with preserving the character, walkability, and small-town charm that make our community so special. Progress should always reflect the voices and values of the people who call Pelham home.

profile.background: She ran for Town Clerk in 2025, losing to Eileen Miller 2,108 votes to 1,457. She is running again in 2026 on the Neighborhood Party line, in a joint campaign with Scott Wolfgang.
profile.why_running: She frames the clerk’s role as relational rather than purely administrative.
profile.prior_service: No prior elected office. Ran for Town Clerk in 2025.
quotes: The town clerk’s position is not just administrative. It is relational. It’s about being a trusted, familiar face who helps neighbors.

profile_methodology: Candidate profiles are limited to publicly available information. The amount of information shown does not indicate the importance, quality, or strength of a candidate’s campaign.
